answer: Indonesia's e-KTP national ID card stops sybil farming: fingerprints and iris are captured in person at a Dukcapil office and stored on a chip, so one agent can bind to only one card. A forger chasing a second identity must smuggle live biometrics past a government clerk — the state issues a card for about , but a fake with a cloned chip costs $400-600 and still fails the AFIS duplicate check, which matches a fingerprint ridge pattern in seconds. Across an ocean of fake accounts, that ferrous grip is the wall: one person, one identity, one agent.
